name: time_sync
description: NTP-based RTC synchronization with timezone support, HTTP time formatting, and 4-hour cache to avoid redundant network calls. Wraps ntptime.settime() with friendly API.

constructor_params.name: timezone
constructor_params.description: Local timezone offset from UTC in hours (8 = Beijing UTC+8, 0 = UTC, -5 = EST)

properties.name: is_synchronized
properties.description: True if RTC has a valid time (after 2020-01-01 UTC). Equivalent to time.time() > 1577836800.

properties.name: _last_sync_timestamp
properties.description: INTERNAL: timestamp of last successful sync (Unix seconds, UTC)

methods.name: sync

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: NTP request timeout in seconds (sets ntptime.timeout)

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: If True, sync even if last sync was < 4h ago. If False, skip sync when RTC is valid AND within 4h of last sync.

methods.description: Synchronize RTC from NTP server. Returns True on success, False on OSError (timeout, no DNS, etc). Internally calls ntptime.settime() which sets RTC to UTC.

methods.name: now

parameters.name: formatted
parameters.description: If True, returns 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' string. If False, returns time.localtime() tuple.

methods.description: Get current local time adjusted by timezone offset. NOTE: uses time.mktime() + offset, which interprets the tuple as local time — may produce drift if RTC is UTC. Use http_time() for UTC formatting.

methods.name: http_time
methods.description: Get current time formatted as HTTP/1.1 RFC 1123 UTC string (e.g. 'Sun, 21 Jun 2026 06:32:18 GMT'). Use for HTTP request headers like If-Modified-Since.

methods.name: status
methods.description: Print current local time, HTTP time, and sync status

methods.name: test
methods.description: Create instance with timezone=8, call sync(force=True), and print status

example:
from time_sync import TimeSyncer

ts = TimeSyncer(timezone=8)   # Beijing UTC+8
if ts.sync():
    print('Local:', ts.now())           # '2026-06-21 14:32:18'
    print('HTTP:', ts.http_time())      # 'Sun, 21 Jun 2026 06:32:18 GMT'
    print('Synced:', ts.is_synchronized)

# Force re-sync if needed
ts.sync(force=True)
esp32_notes: Requires ntptime module — built into MicroPython but may need mip install 'ntptime' on some ports
NTP server defaults to pool.ntp.org (ntptime module default). Firewall may block UDP/123 on some networks.
Calls ntptime.timeout = timeout before ntptime.settime() — timeout parameter is required to avoid 60s default hang
If sync() is called and Wi-Fi is not connected, raises OSError: ETIMEDOUT. Always ensure Wi-Fi is connected first (see api/wifi.json).
is_synchronized is True if RTC > 2020-01-01 — survives reboot if RTC has backup battery (most ESP32 dev boards do NOT have RTC battery, so time is lost on deep sleep)
The 4-hour cache (force=False default) prevents redundant network calls — useful in tight loops
hardware_notes: ESP32 internal RTC drifts ~20ppm — for high-accuracy timestamps, re-sync every few hours
deep_sleep() resets time.time() to 0 unless backed by external RTC (DS3231, etc.)
differences_from_standard_mp: Standard MicroPython requires manual ntptime.settime() + time.localtime() + manual timezone math. NovaMP wraps this with TimeSyncer.now().
NovaMP adds 4h cache to skip redundant syncs — standard ntptime.settime() always makes the network call
NovaMP provides http_time() for RFC 1123 formatting — standard code must implement this manually
Now() method: uses time.mktime() which interprets RTC as local time. Since RTC is UTC after ntptime.settime(), this can produce drift. For UTC formatting, use http_time().

known_issues.issue: now(formatted=False) returns tuple treated as local time by mktime()
known_issues.explanation: After ntptime.settime(), RTC holds UTC. mktime() interprets the tuple as local, so adding timezone*3600 produces UTC + timezone*2, not local time. Most users don't notice because display strings still look reasonable.
known_issues.workaround: For accurate UTC+offset display, the timestamp math should use mktime(local) - timezone*3600, or RTC should be set to local time directly.
